evidence: 2026-09-30: real signup through the Agent Vault proxy using this recipe (MCP session, vault-minted password); all five selectors matched. After the rules were accepted, the form took a public username, the date of birth and the terms checkbox; submit moved to "Confirm email" and "Mastodon: Confirmation instructions for mastodon.social" arrived at the signup address. The account owner opened its link, which showed a CAPTCHA, and completed it. A fresh sign-in with the same credentials was then accepted, with no approval hold.
gotchas: The server's rules are shown first and must be accepted before the form appears (the consent_gate precondition); accepting them is the account owner's agreement.
The form also requires a date of birth (#user_date_of_birth_1i, _2i, _3i), which is the account owner's to supply.
This is the mastodon.social server only; other Mastodon servers are separate sites with their own rules.
The date of birth is three text inputs named in Rails order: #user_date_of_birth_1i is the year, _2i the month, _3i the day.
A terms-of-service and privacy-policy checkbox must be ticked before Sign up.
The emailed confirmation link opens a CAPTCHA before the account is confirmed; both are the account owner's.
